workflow: A traversal obtains a non-owning reference to the current element of a mutable container.
The traversal invokes user-defined comparison or callback logic that mutates the same container and removes the current element.
The removed element is released and deallocated while the traversal or comparison machinery still relies on the retained reference.
A later access uses the freed element, causing a use-after-free and possible process termination instead of a recoverable mutation error.
summary: Reentrant container mutation frees the element being examined
decision_reason: The underlying failure is materially the same as a retained pointer outliving the storage owner: container mutation releases the referenced element before later use. The reentrant callback and container-specific context differ, but the causal mechanism is retained-reference use after owner release.
